name: Waltham
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Waltham, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Waltham, MA: Reagle's ChristmasTime with 100 performers, A Christmas Carol at Gore Place and the Santa Parade to the Common.
lede: Waltham welcomes Santa with a city parade to the Common, then fills December with Reagle's ChristmasTime stage show and Dickens at historic Gore Place.
celebrates: Waltham's season opens with the city's Santa Parade and Holiday Lighting. The mayor and the Fire and Police Departments drive Santa past every elementary school, then the parade ends at City Hall and the Common lights up with music, dancing, hot cocoa from the Salvation Army and visits with Santa. The Waltham Women's Club sets up Santa's mailbox on the Common for children's letters. Indoors, Reagle Music Theatre stages ChristmasTime at the Robinson Theatre with a cast of more than 100, and Gore Place hosts a musical reading of Dickens' A Christmas Carol in its Carriage House.
lastyear: In 2025 the City of Waltham held its Santa Parade and Holiday Lighting on Saturday, November 29, the weekend after Thanksgiving. The community calendar Waltham Times listed it from 2 to 5 pm, with the festivities finishing on Waltham Common at 610 Main Street. Reagle Music Theatre also brought ChristmasTime back to the Robinson Theatre on Lexington Street, where children of all ages were welcome with a ticket of their own.
facts: Waltham helped start the American Industrial Revolution. In 1813 Francis Cabot Lowell and the Boston Associates founded the Boston Manufacturing Company on the Charles River in Waltham, in the mill that now holds the Charles River Museum of Industry and Innovation. Reagle's ChristmasTime is a long tradition too: the show celebrated its 40th year in 2024. Gore Place, where A Christmas Carol is read, is the 1806 country estate of Christopher and Rebecca Gore.
trains: Waltham sits on the MBTA Fitchburg Line, with two Commuter Rail stations in the city: Waltham, near Moody Street and the Common, and Brandeis/Roberts. Trains run to North Station in Boston. Waverley station in neighboring Belmont is also close by. For a holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs a train through the Christmas lights, and the Boston Street Railway Association shares the history of Boston's streetcars.

kidfact: In Waltham, Santa rides with the fire department. He waves from the parade as it passes every elementary school in the city on the way to City Hall.
faq: What is the Waltham Santa Parade?

The City of Waltham's Santa Parade carries Santa around the city with the mayor and the Fire and Police Departments. It passes each elementary school, with designated viewing areas along the route, and ends at City Hall. Santa will not stop at every location, so the city suggests the viewing areas and posts a tracking link on X.
Where is the Waltham holiday lighting?

On Waltham Common, next to City Hall on Main Street. The festivities start with music and dance acts while families wait for Santa to arrive at the end of the parade. The Salvation Army serves hot cocoa, the Common is lit with the flip of a switch, and children can visit Santa for photos afterward.
Where can kids mail a letter to Santa in Waltham?

The Waltham Women's Club sets up Santa's mailbox on Waltham Common during the holiday season. Children can drop off their letters there, and the city asks families to include a return address on each letter so Santa can write back. Letters need to arrive by the city's posted mid December deadline to get an answer before Christmas.
Which train stations are in Waltham?

Waltham has two MBTA Commuter Rail stations on the Fitchburg Line, Waltham and Brandeis/Roberts, with trains to North Station in Boston. Waverley station is just over the line in Belmont. The Waltham stop is the closest to Waltham Common and the Charles River Museum of Industry and Innovation on Moody Street.
